A1.justification: Both PDFs describe 3DMRL. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original molecular interaction and drug-drug interaction experiments, including benchmark comparisons, extrapolation tests, ablations, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds collision diagnostics, configuration sensitivity experiments, and 3D encoder comparisons.

M1.justification: The virtual-environment construction, contrastive alignment, local-frame prediction of normalized interatomic directions, and combined objective are retained. Contrastive/force losses become global/local geometry losses; the added construction variants are experimental controls rather than replacements of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same optical-property, solvation, and DDI tasks, pre-training datasets, and GEOM comparison. The additional experiments reuse existing coverage; filtering molecules for the new 3D encoder comparison changes sample counts rather than introducing a new task or domain.

E2.justification: V2 retains the original architectures and 3D Infomax, GraphMVP, and MoleculeSDE comparisons, then adds evaluated 3D-EMGP, SliDe, and Frad baselines in Appendix E.5/Table 11. This extends comparison to a distinct family of methods that pre-train 3D encoders, although their filtered datasets prevent direct comparison with 3DMRL.

E3.justification: Existing splits, metrics, model configurations, and training settings are retained. The added 3D encoder experiment uses RDKit ETKDG conformers and excludes conversion failures, reducing Absorption from 17,276 to 16,756 pairs, with analogous filtering for Emission and Lifetime. New diagnostics also vary placement rules and molecule counts.

E4.justification: V2 adds collision controls testing radius omission, fixed directions, doubled radius, and collision-free regeneration (Table 3). Appendix E.4 adds sensitivity to target-atom count on DDI tasks and to multiple larger molecules. These substantially expand scrutiny of virtual-environment construction; the earlier loss ablations and environment heatmaps are retained.

E5.justification: The three repetitions of five-fold regression evaluation, five seeded DDI experiments, and existing mean/standard-deviation reporting are retained. New tables provide point estimates but specify no additional uncertainty estimator, significance test, or changed repeated-run protocol.

E6.justification: Previously reported benchmark, extrapolation, GEOM, and loss-ablation scores remain unchanged. Tables 3 and 9-11 add substantial results on collisions, configuration sensitivity, and 3D encoders: for example, collision-free regeneration reports 23.01 minutes/epoch versus 3DMRL's 5.32, with 0% versus 25.12% atomic overlap. The filtered-data 3D encoder scores are new results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, local-frame construction, invariant features, and loss mathematics are retained apart from notation and presentation. V2 adds no theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation; its new force and sampling arguments are qualitative interpretations.

C1.justification: V1's abstract, contribution list, and conclusion emphasize learning intermolecular forces; v2 describes global and local relative geometry, retaining force supervision as an approximate interpretation in Section 4.3. This narrows the claimed physical meaning while preserving the main novelty claim and the 24.93% improvement across 40 tasks.

C2.justification: V2 adds central-force and Lennard-Jones explanations, arguments for randomized initialization, and a collision-versus-computation interpretation. It removes v1's explicit limitations concerning time- and condition-dependent environments and differing force magnitudes, while proposing an MD-trajectory-inspired generator as future work. The physical rationale and qualifications are therefore substantially revised.

D1.justification: V2 documents new placement controls, per-epoch runtimes, and ETKDG conversion-failure counts. Existing architecture, optimization, and software details remain unchanged. It also removes v1's conflicting statement that all computation uses an RTX 3090, retaining the appendix's A6000 pre-training/RTX 3090 downstream allocation.

R1.justification: V2 adds references concerning molecular initialization and sampling, including Packmol and DiffMD, and the newly evaluated 3D encoder methods; several earlier peripheral references disappear. The principal positioning against existing MRL and single-molecule pre-training remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative into Related Works, Preliminaries, Methodology, Experiments, and Conclusion. It rewrites the force/global-local terminology throughout, moves extrapolation to Appendix E.2, adds an explanatory appendix and conference checklist, and removes extended application, impact, and limitations sections.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different conference layout, separates and relabels the framework illustration, splits the original analysis figure, and consolidates environment heatmaps. It merges v1 Tables 2 and 3 into a dense combined table, adds four experimental tables and an MPP-versus-MRL schematic, and relocates the extrapolation display.

improvement.justification: V2 describes the direction-based supervision more precisely as relative geometry and adds useful tests of previously unchecked collision and configuration choices (Table 3 and Appendix E.4), strengthening understanding without altering the main results. The gains are limited by the non-comparable 3D baseline settings and the removal of v1's explicit physical limitations.
